PHSCS 587

Degenerate carrier statistics

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows where the exponential tail ceases to represent an occupied band

Highly occupied bands require the full Fermi–Dirac distribution. For a nondegenerate conduction band, EC lies sufficiently above EF that f(E) is small throughout the important occupied energies. Once EF approaches or enters the band, exclusion limits each spin state’s occupation to one and the exponential approximation loses accuracy.

The reliable general expression is n = ∫EC∞ g(E)/{1 + exp[(E − EF)/(kBT)]} dE. For a parabolic band this can be expressed as a Fermi integral, with its normalization stated explicitly. The figure compares edge occupations rather than integrated carrier densities; it reveals why a Boltzmann prediction above unity cannot describe a state probability.

There is no universal dopant concentration at which every material becomes degenerate. The relevant criterion depends on EF relative to the band edge, the DOS, temperature and ionization. Very heavy doping can additionally alter the band structure through disorder and many-body effects. Those changes are distinct from using the correct occupation distribution for a fixed band.

Example

At EF = EC the exact edge occupation is 1/2, whereas the Boltzmann edge approximation gives 1. An integrated DOS calculation determines the actual carrier concentration.

Practice

1. Which mathematical step remains valid when Boltzmann statistics fail?

Think of the DOS and occupation separately.

Counting states by integrating g(E)f(E) remains valid within the chosen band model. The exact FD occupation replaces the exponential approximation.
